headline: YelpIt User Leaves One-Star Review of the Sun, Calls It 'Too Political'
subheadline: Review goes viral with 10,000 'useful' votes; sun unavailable for comment
summary: A YelpIt review criticizing the sun for being 'overly bright' and 'political' has become the platform's most-interacted-with post this year.
content:
In what may be the most ambitious review in YelpIt history, user GaryFromAccounting has left a scathing one-star review of the sun itself.

"One star. Would give zero if I could," the review begins. "First of all, way too bright. I didn't ask for this. Second, it's everywhere I go. I moved three times and it followed me. That's harassment."

The review, posted to YelpIt's page for "The Sun (Celestial Body)," has accumulated over 10,000 "useful" votes and sparked a debate about the boundaries of customer feedback.

"It's clearly just being political at this point," the review continues. "Why does it have to be in the sky EVERY day? Some of us prefer clouds. But no, the sun has an agenda and it's not subtle about it."

GaryFromAccounting rates the sun poorly across all categories: one star for "Ambiance" ("blindingly aggressive"), one star for "Value" ("I don't remember signing up for this"), and one star for "Service" ("gave me a sunburn in 2019 and never apologized").

The review concludes: "The moon is right there and it has the decency to take days off. The sun could learn something about work-life balance."

YelpIt has declined to remove the review, stating it "meets community guidelines" and that "the sun has not claimed its business page to respond."

Reach out was attempted to the sun for comment, but it remained silent, continuing to just sit there, being bright, as if proving GaryFromAccounting's point.

At press time, 847 other users had checked in to the sun's YelpIt page, with one marking it as "good for kids."
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
